top.author: @gracebe235
top.text: My dad was a fireman many years ago. He was big on educating us on these sorts of things. I NEVER leave the toaster plugged in….it is unplugged as soon as the bread is buttered. Occasionally, my husband will leave it plugged in, I always remind him when he does. I was taught that simple appliances like toaster ovens, irons, and blenders, should never be left plugged in either. I just unplug ALL simple appliances that are not in use…..even my sewing machine. Also, things that are plugged in, can sometimes be damaged in a power surge when the electricity goes out, and comes back on.

newest.author: @jld0001967
newest.text:
I am phobic about unplugging the toaster oven.  On the basic, cheaper toaster ovens (that I like bc they’re smaller), the dials can be jiggly.  Someone might turn the bottom dial for toast and also the top dial for oven.  One shuts off short-term. The other stays on.  And oven cycles on/off to maintain temps, so you may not see the burning elements glowing orange. 

People also dont pull their toasters out from under their cabinets and heat gets trapped and stuff can fall behind it.

*Toaster, any appliance that produces heat
*Extension cord under a rug, trapped heat
*Power strip plugged into a power strip! 
(If strip strip feels warm - replace it) 
*Clothes dryer - NOT overnight, NOT when asleep, NOT when away from home. 
*DON’T : electric scooters etc charging overnight /only when at home & awake
*Hair styling heating tools 
*Space heater in bedroom - OFF overnight! 
*Electric blanket/mats - warm bed, turn off before sleep or use auto shut off
*Phone or tablet charging UNDER a pillow overnight
*Anything plugged in that is WARM, HOT, DISCOLORED.
